objects.name: Analytic 1856
objects.description: Real-time network monitoring identifies a sustained spike in malformed or high-volume Industrial Control System (ICS) protocol traffic directed at a single field device from a source not in the approved control server list, immediately followed by that device dropping out of the supervisory poll cycle. Documented precedent: Sandworm's Industroyer malware sent a crafted 18-byte proprietary User Datagram Protocol (UDP) packet to port 50000 on Siemens Protection Technology (SIPROTEC) relays (CVE-2015-5374), causing the device to hang and require a manual reboot. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when a device-specific traffic/resource threshold is exceeded and the same window shows service degradation, failed polling, device alarm/restart, resource exhaustion, or malformed/out-of-spec protocol behavior. Suppress planned load tests, maintenance, network convergence/failover, and known equipment faults after operator confirmation.

x_mitre_mutable_elements.description: Network device CPU utilization percentage above which sustained load suggests packet-processing strain from flood traffic.
Connections-per-minute threshold exceeding normal SCADA polling cadence, derived from the device's actual configured scan rate.
Time window over which flood rate and subsequent device silence are correlated, typically 1-5 minutes.
Device-specific supervisory poll interval used to determine what counts as a process historian gap.
Deviation from baseline interface error/discard rate, tuned against historical interface health data.
Number of malformed/out-of-spec PDUs within the detection window constituting a flood, set above the device's documented error-tolerance baseline.
